finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[RT-1] Unbounded client-to-everyone data fan-out
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L220)
Evidence: The controller publishes position and animation payloads via localParticipant.publishData on a fixed 100ms interval (two channels => ~20 messages/sec/client) with DataPacket_Kind.LOSSY and no recipient filtering or interest management. This produces N producers × N recipients fan-out proportional to room size.  
Impact: At scale this will saturate LiveKit/network bandwidth and CPU (quadratic message growth), causing dropped packets, increased latency, or LiveKit/client disconnects.  
Fix: Reduce frequency and switch to interest management (proximity/zone-based routing), aggregate/encode deltas, or server-side partitioning (shards/regions) to limit fan-out.

[RT-2] Stateless lossy updates with no replay or sequencing
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L220)
Evidence: Position/animation are sent LOSSY without sequence numbers, ACKs, or any server-side authoritative snapshot; client state is kept only in-memory and remote state is reconstructed purely from live data channel events.  
Impact: Clients that reconnect or experience packet loss receive stale/incomplete state (desynced worlds) and there is no reliable catch-up mechanism, breaking correctness for collision/interaction logic.  
Fix: Introduce authoritative state snapshots (server or persistent store), sequence numbers/versions for data messages, or a join-time state replay endpoint so reconnecting clients can catch up.

[RT-3] Unrestricted guest token issuance enabling abuse
File: src/pages/api/connection_details.ts (L1-L160)
Evidence: If is_universe_guest is set, the route issues LiveKit AccessTokens and returns ws_url/token without auth or rate limiting.  
Impact: Attackers or runaway clients can request many tokens and open many LiveKit connections, leading to connection exhaustion and billing/usage spikes on the media server.  
Fix: Require server-side rate limits, CAPTCHAs, per-IP/tenant quotas, or attestation before issuing guest tokens; revoke/monitor suspicious token issuance.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[RT-4] Expensive listRooms() per-request and optimistic success on errors
File: src/app/api/check-universe/route.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: The endpoint calls roomService.listRooms() on each GET and, on any LiveKit error or missing service, sets livekitRoomExists = true (assumes LiveKit success).  
Impact: Frequent checks will trigger heavy LiveKit API traffic and can hit provider rate limits; the optimistic fallback can falsely allow joins to non-existent LiveKit rooms, causing downstream join errors.  
Fix: Use targeted queries (getRoom or room name lookup), cache room existence with TTL, and fail-safe (return unknown/deny) instead of optimistic true on LiveKit errors.

[RT-5] Webhook DB updates on high churn may become a hotspot
File: src/app/api/webhooks/livekit/route.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: LiveKit webhooks increment/decrement currentUsers and toggle isLive using direct DB updates on every participant_joined/left event.  
Impact: Rooms with high join/leave churn can generate many sequential DB writes, causing contention or throttling on the database and delayed realtime state visibility.  
Fix: Batch or debounce webhook updates, use an increment queue or lightweight cache (Redis) for high-frequency counters, and persist periodically.

--- INFO ---

[RT-6] Socket.IO present in package.json but unused
File: package.json / repo tree
Evidence: Dependencies include socket.io and socket.io-client, but codebase uses LiveKit (no socket.io imports found).
